industry: Consumer Packaged Goods / Specialty Food & Beverage
businessModel: Branded refrigerated cold-brew and functional coffee beverage maker selling DTC, regional grocery, and national natural-channel retail
businessStage: Scale-up, Series A funded, transitioning from DTC-led to retail-led distribution
sourceNote: Real-world pattern from emerging refrigerated CPG beverage brands (mirrors public disclosures and trade-press patterns from refrigerated coffee/functional-beverage challengers such as the Califia/High Brew/Chameleon cohort). Reflects the documented CPG scale-up trap where reported retail revenue grows fast but gross-to-net erosion from trade spend, slotting, refrigerated freight, spoilage, and broker fees collapses contribution margin. Metrics reflect typical natural-channel refrigerated SKU economics and IRI/SPINS-style velocity benchmarks.

ownerIntake.businessType: Refrigerated cold-brew and adaptogen-functional coffee brand, founded 2019. 9 SKUs in 12oz and 32oz refrigerated formats. $14.2M gross (invoiced) revenue TTM. 38 employees. Distribution: ~2,400 retail doors (natural channel + regional conventional grocery), DTC subscription (~9,000 active subscribers), and Amazon. Co-packed at two refrigerated facilities; no owned manufacturing.
ownerIntake.stage: Scale-up Series A ($11M raised 2022): Invoiced revenue $14.2M TTM growing 41% YoY, but net revenue (after trade/returns/slotting) only $9.8M. Reported gross margin on invoiced basis 34%, but true contribution margin after trade spend, freight, and spoilage is 11% and falling (was 19% twelve months ago, -800bps). Monthly burn $420k. Cash on hand $3.1M. DTC contribution margin 44%; retail contribution margin now 4%.
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Reach contribution-margin breakeven (>20% blended contribution margin) and a defensible path to profitability within 9 months to unlock a $6M bridge/Series A extension from existing investors.
ownerConstraints: Cash runway 7.4 months at current $420k/month burn; bridge financing is conditional on a credible margin-recovery plan.

Trade spend has grown to 18% of invoiced retail revenue (slotting, scan-down promos, free-fill), versus 9% twelve months ago; two national retailers demand 15%+ promotional frequency to retain shelf space.
Refrigerated DSD/LTL freight runs $0.62/unit and spoilage/short-code returns are 7% of retail shipments due to 90-day code life and slow velocity in newer doors.
Co-pack minimum runs are 8,000 units/SKU; cannot economically reduce SKU count below current run minimums without renegotiation.
Founder has signed 12-month shelf commitments with two national natural retailers (~600 doors) that carry guaranteed promo calendars and cannot be exited without penalty until Q1 next year.
Team is lean (38 people, only 2 in finance/FP&A); no SKU-level or door-level contribution reporting exists today.
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: Invoiced revenue is up 41% YoY but the company is burning faster than ever and true contribution margin has fallen from 19% to 11% in twelve months. The founder cannot tell whether the brand is fundamentally unprofitable, whether specific channels/SKUs/doors are dragging the blend, or whether trade spend is buying unprofitable distribution. Investors will not release the bridge without a credible margin story within 60 days.

businessProblem: A refrigerated cold-brew CPG brand is growing invoiced revenue 41% YoY while its true contribution margin has collapsed from 19% to 11% in twelve months, and burn is at an all-time high with 7.4 months of runway. Reported (invoiced) gross margin of 34% masks a much weaker net picture once trade spend (now 18% of retail revenue), refrigerated freight, slotting, and 7% spoilage are subtracted, leaving retail contribution at just 4% versus DTC at 44%. The founder must determine whether the business is fundamentally unprofitable, whether the retail channel as a whole destroys value, or whether a specific subset of SKUs and low-velocity doors is dragging an otherwise viable blend — before committing to any retail retreat, SKU rationalization, or price action that could breach shelf commitments or co-pack minimums.

evidence.finding: Invoiced revenue grew 41% YoY to $14.2M, but net revenue is only $9.8M and true blended contribution margin fell from 19% to 11% over twelve months (-800bps) even as the top line accelerated. The divergence between invoiced growth and contribution decline indicates revenue is being bought with margin, not earned through profitable demand.
evidence.source: Management P&L, gross-to-net reconciliation, trailing-twelve-month financials

evidence.finding: Channel contribution margins diverge sharply: DTC contribution is 44% while retail contribution is just 4%. Retail doors grew from 1,300 to 2,400 in twelve months — nearly all of the contribution erosion coincides with the door expansion, and the new doors are concentrated in the lower-velocity natural channel.
evidence.source: Channel P&L breakdown, distribution expansion log

evidence.finding: Trade spend has doubled from 9% to 18% of invoiced retail revenue in twelve months, refrigerated freight is $0.62/unit, and spoilage/short-code returns run 7% of retail shipments due to 90-day code life colliding with slow velocity in newer doors. There is no door-level velocity or SKU-level contribution reporting to attribute where the spend and spoilage are concentrated.
evidence.source: Trade-spend ledger, freight invoices, returns/credits log, FP&A note on reporting gaps

evidence.finding: DTC subscriber base is flat at ~9,000 and DTC contribution remains strong at 44%, indicating brand demand and product quality are healthy where the brand controls economics. NPS and repeat rates on DTC are stable. The deterioration is therefore not a demand or product-quality problem; it tracks the shift in revenue mix toward subsidized retail distribution.
evidence.source: DTC subscription analytics, repeat-purchase cohort data
